text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures retain losses through the session, lacking necessary spark to move higher, with more activity at short end as investors shift away from the U.S. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.82, down 0/11 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended the day down as strong M4 data and gloomy Europe took its toll, almost all Thursday's gains wiped out, traders said with auction due and not much data next week, few want to end Friday long. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-23/32, down 14/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures settled lower as ongoing speculation about the prospect of an early election or cabinet reshuffle buffeted bonds throughout the session. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.72, down 0.18 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - The Italian debt market closed down but off session lows after an erratic, volatile day dominated by uncertainty and conflicting talk over Italy's early EMU membership. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.74, down 0.63 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries remained higher following Michigan data, with Michigan sentiment rises slightly, but report mixed, with the market seen remaining in narrow trading range, short-covering and technicals seen as dominant activities. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-30/32, up 02/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.07 percent.

JAPAN - Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Tokyo trade higher, ignoring comments by a senior Finance Ministry official who termed the JGB market "bubbly". In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.82, up 0.04 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - A debut sovereign Eurobond offering from Ecuador enlivened an otherwise routine pre-weekend session. Ecuador's offering was a larger than expected $500 million deal in two tranches lead managed by Chase. The size compared to the $400 million being touted Thursday and the $300 million previously expected. There is a $350 million five-year fixed-rate leg to be priced 470 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, the other a $150 million seven-year FRN to pay six-month LIBOR plus 475 b.p.
